description.value: The study investigated neural responses to subliminal and supraliminal sexual images using fMRI, including image-type by presentation-level interactions and gender-specific analyses.

spans.text: The present work was set to extend existing findings by investigating the neural mechanisms underlying the different responses to subliminal vs. supraliminal stimuli

description.value: Participants completed an event-related fMRI experiment involving sexual and neutral primes presented at subliminal or supraliminal levels.

spans.text: The experiment was divided into four blocks of trials.
To be able to maintain a consistent design across both subliminal and supraliminal presentation conditions, we embedded the sexual cues (as primes before each trial) within a cognitive task

Exposure to supraliminal sexual images was associated with higher activation in both arousal-related areas and control-related areas, whereas subliminal exposure was associated mainly with activation in arousal-related areas.

value: Exposure to the supraliminal sexual images as compared with exposure to subliminal sexual images was associated with higher activation in the insula, inferior and middle occipital, precentral gyrus, cuneus and precuneus. It was also associated with higher activation in IFG, cingulate gyrus, SFG, medial and middle frontal gyri, parahippocampal gyrus and the culmen.
Subliminal exposure to the sexual image did not result in any increased activation at the P < 0.001 level in comparison to supraliminal exposure.

value: For women, the supraliminal sexual images resulted in higher activation in the ACC, cingulate gyrus, IFG, middle frontal and SFG. In addition there was activation in the caudate, globus pallidus, inferior occipital, superior and middle temporal gyri, supramarginal gyrus and inferior parietal.

definition.value: supraliminal sexual > neutral contrast for men

value: The same contrast for men showed increased activation in the IFG, ACC and cingulate, culmen, globus pallidus, and in the SFG/middle frontal. Men also had activation in the thalamus, insula, caudate, supramarginal gyrus and putamen.

definition.value: subliminal sexual > neutral contrast for women

value: When exposed to subliminal sexual images, women showed higher activation in the inferior parietal, putamen, insula and inferior, medial and superior frontal gyri. Women also had activation in the cingulate, posterior cingulate, precentral gyrus, cuneus, precuneus, culmen, parahippocampal gyrus, superior temporal and inferior and superior parietal.

definition.value: subliminal sexual > neutral contrast for men

value: Men, on the other hand, did not show higher activation in any area at the P < 0.001 threshold.

name.value: Subliminal and supraliminal sexual and neutral picture prime liking task

description.value: Event-related cognitive task in which sexual or neutral prime images were presented subliminally or supraliminally before abstract target images.

design_type.value: Event-related design with a 2 × 2 within-subjects factorial structure and gender as a between-subjects variable

instructions.value: Participants rated as quickly as possible how much they liked each target image using one of five buttons, from 1 (do not like it at all) to 5 (like it very much).

stimuli.value: Abstract target images preceded by sexual or neutral prime images, with forward and backward masks; sexual primes were presented subliminally or supraliminally.

value: button_press
Liking rating from 1 to 5
